title: RABVA: Rendering Arabic Script Correctly
description: Arabic text broke in unexpected ways: words stacked one per line, erab marks changed character counts, and Safari rendered layouts differently from Chrome. I learned how right-to-left text, font metrics and browser quirks interact, and fixed each case with targeted CSS and data normalization.

title: RABVA: Two Scripts, One Data Model
description: The Quran text exists in Uthmani and Simple script, and words are split into sub-words. Designing a database that keeps both in sync, with a permanent relation table between ayah-words and whole-words, took several iterations and careful indexing to stay fast.

title: RABVA: Drag-Scroll and Continuous Reading
description: Building a reading view that scrolls continuously through Uthmani pages, remembers the exact ayah you were on, prefetches the next page and still works with swipe on mobile exposed a lot of edge cases in scroll handling, especially on large screens.

title: RABVA: Root Search in Tabs
description: Letting users open many root searches at once meant the search module had to be shared between the reading view and the Canvas without duplicating code. Getting the tab state, URL sharing and the table overflow right was a real exercise in component design.

title: RABVA: Multilingual Interface
description: The UI had to work in thirteen languages, three of them right-to-left. Instead of translating word by word, every string became a translation key stored in the database, with rules for RTL text that flips the text direction but not the layout or icons.

title: RABVA: Running Many Docker Stacks at Once
description: Several branches were developed in parallel, so each needed its own isolated backend, frontend and database. I set up branch-named Docker Compose stacks seeded from a database export so nothing collided with the main local environment.

title: RABVA: Byte-Exact Arabic Database Exports
description: A plain mysqldump silently corrupted some Arabic characters. I built an export pipeline that enforces utf8mb4 end to end and a diagnostic script that catches charset problems before they reach another environment.

title: RABVA: Production on AWS with Nginx and HTTPS
description: I moved the app to an EC2 instance managed with Terraform, with staging and production kept completely separate, the React build served as static files by Nginx inside Docker, and Let's Encrypt certificates renewing automatically.

title: RABVA: A 3D View of the Quran
description: As an experiment I built a proof of concept that shows surahs as stacked 3D layers of ayahs and words you can rotate, zoom and fly through, using react-force-graph-3d with the Arabic words drawn as flat text planes in 3D space.

title: Deploying My Portfolio on AWS EC2 🔥
description: Deploying my portfolio on AWS EC2 was a complex but rewarding process. I configured the EC2 instance, set up Node.js and Nginx, managed file permissions, and troubleshot deployment issues. Connecting my project to GitHub allowed for easy updates. Overcoming challenges like SSH authentication, firewall rules, and static file access gave me hands-on experience with cloud hosting and server management.

title: Migrating My App’s Database
description: I worked on moving my app's database from MongoDB to  MySQL, which involved updating some of the server-side code and adjusting the queries to make everything work smoothly.

title: Using useRef in React
description: I faced a challenge while working with useRef to persist values across renders without causing unnecessary re-renders, but I learned a lot through experimenting with it.

title: Implementing OAuth
description: I worked on adding OAuth authentication to my app, which was tricky at first, but it’s been really useful for securing user login.

title: Fixing Bugs with useEffect
description: I had to troubleshoot some issues with state management and useEffect in my app to make sure the suggestion page worked as expected.

title: Learning MySQL
description: I spent some time improving my skills with MySQL, adding new fields to tables and making sure everything was connected properly with foreign keys.

title: Deploying My Project
description: I successfully deployed my front-end on Netlify and my back-end on Heroku for my capstone project, which was a pretty rewarding experience.

title: Integrating Google Maps
description: I figured out how to use the Google Maps API in my app to show nearby providers based on specific information like postal codes and benefit types.

title: Building a Quiz App with Students
description: I helped my students create a quiz app where users could pick their own TV channels. It was a great way to practice React and state management.

title: Finding a Free Database
description: I initially thought I found a free database to deploy my app, only to get a bill later. It taught me a lot about researching and understanding database pricing before committing.

title: Organizing My Code
description: I made sure to keep my code organized across my UI and API repositories so that everything was clean and easy to manage.
